name: reparenting under a descendant is refused as a loop even when a rank re-definition made it rank-legal
notes: The rank re-definition is the point. Types are events and the last definition wins, so moving `phase` from rank 1 to rank 3 puts it BELOW the `step` it already contains — after which the loop-closing reparent is rank-legal and nothing but the ancestor walk refuses it. Without the second definition the fixture would still refuse `hierarchy.cycle` — the walk sits ABOVE rank, and a loop is named as a loop even when the rank is also violated — but it would prove nothing, because DELETING the walk would then leave the rank check refusing (1 under 2), and a planted defect that swaps one refusal for another cannot show the walk was the only thing standing. The re-definition is what turns the mutation into a clean ACCEPTANCE. The re-definition is a PRIOR, so it is never itself evaluated: priorEvents are the accepted past.

expected.reason: This move would put the ticket inside one of its own sub-items, making a loop. A ticket cannot contain itself.
